title: The Role of Sound on Spirituality in Religious Environments and Islamic Architecture by Using EEG
research_question: To investigate the effects of sound pressure level on mosque users' brain waves (alpha waves and theta/beta ratio) in the interior of the Nasir al-Mulk mosque in Shiraz, and how this relates to spiritual sense.

participants.description: Part 1 (survey): 64 experts (21 females, 43 males) including professors, associate professors, assistant professors, postdoctoral researchers, and doctoral researchers in Islamic architectural engineering and acoustics. Part 2/3 (EEG lab): 23 people (14 men, 9 women) aged 17-39 years old.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Adhan sound at 6 different sound pressure levels (30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 dBC).
360-degree image of the main Shabistan of Nasir al-Mulk Mosque in Shiraz, Iran, shown through virtual reality glasses.
Gray image shown during brain recovery periods to neutralize mental effects.

measures.construct: Ranking of sound characteristics for spiritual sense
Brain activity related to tranquility and spiritual sense
measures.instrument: Electroencephalogram (EEG) measuring alpha waves and theta/beta ratio

mechanisms: Increased alpha brain waves and decreased theta/beta ratio are associated with enhanced tranquility and spiritual sense.
Multisensory integration of visual architectural cues and auditory stimuli (Adhan) influences brain wave patterns related to spiritual experience.
implementation_implications: Architectural design of religious places should consider sound pressure level (specifically 40-45 dB for Adhan) to enhance spiritual sense and tranquility.
Qualitative aspects of sound, beyond mere quantitative use, should be integrated into architectural design to improve interior quality and spiritual experience.

limitations: The tests were carried out in a virtual reality environment rather than the real environment of the Nasir al-Mulk Mosque, which may affect the accuracy and scientific validity of the results.
